title: Trading Policy (Schedule 10 to the Corporate Governance Plan)

tiers.name: Key Management Personnel
tiers.description: Persons having authority and responsibility for planning, directing and controlling the activities of the entity, determined by the Company to be its Directors, executives and those employees directly reporting to the Managing Director.

tiers.name: Chair of the Board
tiers.description: The Chair of the Board; distinguished only because his or her own dealing approval must come from the Board rather than from the Chair.

tiers.name: Associates
tiers.description: Nominees, agents or other associates of Key Management Personnel, such as family members, family trusts and family companies; dealings through them are treated as the Key Management Personnel's own for insider trading and notification purposes.

windows.start_anchor: two weeks prior to release of the Company's Annual Report
windows.end_anchor: 48 hours after the release of the Company's Annual Report

windows.start_anchor: two weeks prior to release of the Half Year Report
windows.end_anchor: 48 hours after the release of the Half Year Report

windows.start_anchor: two weeks prior to release of the Company's quarterly reports (if applicable)
windows.end_anchor: 48 hours after the release of the Company's quarterly reports

rules.detail: The Policy never mentions derivatives, options over securities (other than the Company's own employee option scheme), or other financial products created over the Company's shares.
No reference to hedging, economic risk, or limiting exposure to equity incentives anywhere in the Policy.
Prepaid forwards or other monetisation structures are not addressed.

Short selling is not named. Any 'sale' of the Company's securities requires prior written approval of the Chair of the Board or the Board, is barred in Closed Periods absent exceptional circumstances, and cannot occur while holding price sensitive information; a short sale would fall within these general terms.
rules.evidence: Any Key Management Personnel ... wishing to buy, sell or exercise rights in relation to the Company's securities must obtain the prior written approval of the Chair of the Board or the Board before doing so.

rules.detail: Securities lending is not mentioned anywhere in the Policy.
CFDs are not mentioned and 'securities' is not defined to extend to financial products referencing the Company's shares.

Margin lending is named as an example of a secured lender arrangement; a disposal of securities resulting from the lender exercising its rights on default is a permitted exception available 'at any time' (including in a Closed Period) and expressly does not breach insider trading laws. Entering into the loan itself is not addressed as requiring prior approval.
rules.evidence: dispose of securities of the Company resulting from a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement

rules.detail: Granting security over the Company's securities is not itself listed as a dealing requiring approval; the Policy assumes shares may be provided as security and only regulates the resulting sale on default.
rules.evidence: Where Company securities are provided to a lender as security by way of mortgage or charge, a sale that occurs under that mortgage or charge as a consequence of default would not breach insider trading laws.

rules.detail: Margin lending is given only 'for example' of a secured lender arrangement, indicating the exception is not limited to margin loans but extends to secured financing generally.
rules.evidence: dispose of securities of the Company resulting from a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement

rules.detail: Blanket discouragement of short-term trading with no defined holding period; only carve-out is selling shares shortly after exercising options.
rules.evidence: Key Management Personnel should never engage in short-term trading of the Company's securities except for the exercise of options where the shares will be sold shortly thereafter.

clearance.approver: Chair of the Board or the Board
clearance.post_trade_deadline: within two (2) business days of the transaction occurring
clearance.evidence: Any Key Management Personnel (other than the Chair of the Board) wishing to buy, sell or exercise rights in relation to the Company's securities must obtain the prior written approval of the Chair of the Board or the Board before doing so.

clearance.post_trade_deadline: within two (2) business days of the transaction occurring
clearance.evidence: If the Chair of the Board wishes to buy, sell or exercise rights in relation to the Company's securities, the Chair of the Board must obtain the prior approval of the Board before doing so.

carve_outs: exercise of options where the shares will be sold shortly thereafter
short_term.evidence: Key Management Personnel should never engage in short-term trading of the Company's securities except for the exercise of options where the shares will be sold shortly thereafter.

exceptions.evidence: acquire ordinary shares in the Company by conversion of securities giving a right of conversion to ordinary shares
acquire Company securities under a dividend reinvestment, or top-up plan that is available to all holders or securities of the same class
acquire, or agree to acquire or exercise options under an employee incentive scheme
make an investment in, or trade in units of, a fund or other scheme ... where the assets of the fund or other scheme are invested at the discretion of a third party

trade in the securities of the Company by that trust, provided the restricted person is not a beneficiary of the trust and any decision to trade during a prohibited period is taken by the other trustees or by the investment managers independently
undertake to accept, or accept, a takeover offer

trade under an offer or invitation made to all or most of the security holders, such as a rights issue, a security purchase plan, a dividend or distribution reinvestment plan and an equal access buy-back, where the plan ... has been approved by the Board
dispose of securities of the Company resulting from a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement
exercise (but not sell securities following exercise) an option or a right under an employee incentive scheme ... where the final date for the exercise ... falls during a prohibited period
trade under a non-discretionary trading plan for which prior written clearance has been provided in accordance with procedures set out in this Policy

exceptions.approver: Managing Director (or all other members of the Board, if the applicant is the Managing Director)
exceptions.evidence: Key Management Personnel who are not in possession of inside information ... may be given prior written clearance ... to sell or otherwise dispose of Company securities in a Closed Period where the person is in severe financial hardship

exceptions.approver: Managing Director (or all other members of the Board, if the applicant is the Managing Director)
exceptions.evidence: Exceptional circumstances may apply to the disposal of Company securities by a Key Management Personnel if the person is required by a court order or a court enforceable undertaking ... to transfer or sell securities

exemption_authority: The Managing Director (or, if the applicant is the Managing Director, all other Board members) may grant a written exemption from a Closed Period for severe financial hardship or exceptional circumstances (e.g. court order), specifying the time period during which the sale may occur; confidentiality of the exemption is not addressed. The Company may separately vary the Closed Period rule generally by announcement to all Key Management Personnel.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Key Management Personnel may at any time dispose of securities of the Company resulting from a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement ... a sale that occurs under that mortgage or charge as a consequence of default would not breach insider trading laws.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A bank's enforcement sale of the collared shares on default is expressly excepted from the Closed Periods and from the insider trading prohibition, which is favourable for the secured loan leg of a funded collar.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the management of the sale of any significant volume of Company securities (ie a volume ... in excess of 10% of the total securities held by the seller ... or ... in excess of 10% of the average daily traded volume ... for the preceding 20 trading days) ... needs to be discussed with the Board and the Company's legal advisers prior to the execution of any sale.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: If the collar or its unwind involves delivering more than 10% of the executive's holding or of 20-day average volume, a mandatory Board and legal-adviser discussion (with a documented file note) precedes execution, adding process and potential delay for the bank.

bespoke_clauses.clause: it is not permissible to provide the exercise price of options by selling the shares acquired on the exercise of these options unless the sale of those shares occurs outside the periods specified in paragraph 4.1.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: If the collar structure is layered onto option-exercise shares, a cashless/sell-to-cover exercise must be timed outside the Closed Periods.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Policy defines covered transactions only as 'the sale and purchase of any securities of the Company' and never addresses derivatives, hedging or CFDs.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An OTC put and call are not expressly named, so whether they are caught depends on whether 'securities' or 'dealing' is read broadly; the bank should have the company confirm treatment before relying on the absence of an express rule.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The insider trading prohibition extends to dealings by individuals through nominees, agents or other associates, such as family members, family trusts and family companies (referred to as "Associates").
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Routing the collar or the secured loan through a family trust or company does not avoid the approval and notification requirements.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The ASX Listing Rules require the Company to notify the ASX within 5 business days after any dealing in securities of the Company ... which results in a change in the relevant interests of a Director.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Granting security over the shares to the bank, or settling the collar, may change the Director's relevant interest and trigger an Appendix 3Y disclosure within 5 business days.

summary: A funded collar is workable in principle for a VMM Key Management Personnel, though several process steps apply. The Policy does not name derivatives, hedging or short selling, so an OTC put and call are not expressly addressed, but the general requirement of prior written approval from the Chair of the Board or the Board (post-trade notification to the Company Secretary within 2 business days) would likely apply if entry, adjustment or unwind is treated as dealing in, or a change in relevant interest over, the underlying shares. Secured financing is favourably treated: margin lending is given only as an example of a permitted secured lender arrangement, and a forced sale on the lender's enforcement is an exception available 'at any time', including during a Closed Period, and does not breach insider trading laws — supporting the loan leg of the collar even through a Closed Period on default. Voluntary entry, adjustment and unwind should still occur outside the Closed Periods (two weeks before to 48 hours after annual, half-year and quarterly reports) and while the executive holds no inside information. If the collared shares exceed 10% of the executive's holding or of 20-day average trading volume, the transaction must first be discussed with the Board and the company's legal advisers, and the bank should have the company confirm how it treats the derivative legs themselves.
